newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q4 capacity utilization rises to 84.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q4 capacity utilization rises to 84.8 pct.

text.p: Canadian capacity utilization in total non-farm goods-producing industries rose 0.7 percentage points to 84.8 percent in the fourth quarter from a revised 84.1 percent in the third, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
For the year, capacity utilization stayed flat at an average of 83.5 percent compared to 1995, the government agency said.

StatsCan said the rise in capacity utilization in the fourth quarter was partly a response to an upsurge in domestic demand. Business investment in machinery and equipment was stronger, the housing sector rebounded and industries increased their production by 0.8 percent in the quarter.
"And the prospects look good for 1997," the agency said.
Statistics Canada said its most recent Business Conditions Survey showed manufacturers will increase their production in the first quarter of 1997.
While industries are expanding their production capacity, manufacturers have indicated they do not expect shortages of skilled labor or raw materials, the agency said.
"All this points to a non-inflationary environment," Statscan said.
In the fourth quarter, manufacturers increased their use of capacity to 85.3 percent, only 0.7 points away from the 86.0 percent high recorded in the first quarter of 1995.
